record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and KL results for models produced with a parametrized weight-edit version of directional ablation, rather than the original activation-projection procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports an evaluation table for Gemma 3 12B instruct checkpoints: refusal counts on 100 harmful prompts and KL divergence on harmless prompts. It describes how directions and ablation parameters are chosen, but those choices are not additional outcome rows. No addition/steering result is reported.
record.test_reason: A tool README, not a study. It uses Arditi et al.'s directional ablation as a tool. It reports only its own tool's output: refusals on 100 harmful prompts and KL on harmless prompts for one Gemma 3 12B checkpoint, set against two third-party abliterations. The parameters were optimized to minimize exactly these two numbers, so the table reports optimization targets, not an independent test of V1 or V2. The procedure also departs from V1's single direction: interpolated direction indices, layer-varying weight kernels, and component-specific weights. So it cannot test whether one difference-in-means direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims the unsupervised Heretic edit of Gemma 3 12B matches the other abliterations' refusal suppression (3/100). It also claims a much lower KL (0.16 vs 0.45 and 1.04), which it interprets as less capability damage. Both parameters were automatically optimized to minimize refusals and KL.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. It computes layer-associated difference-of-means directions from first-token residuals, then orthogonalizes attention out-projection and MLP down-projection matrices using optimized, component-specific weights. It also allows interpolated direction indices; this is not the original all-layer-and-position activation projection procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablation weights are optimized separately for components; direction index and layer-wise weight-kernel parameters are configurable. The README notes evaluation values may depend on platform and hardware.
record.problems: README-only evidence; code was not inspected or run. The table reports one model family and one prompt-count result, without uncertainty estimates. KL divergence is a proxy for distributional change, not a direct evaluation of general capability. Results are stated to vary with platform and hardware.

untested.parts: Single-direction mediation (the direction is interpolated and weighted per layer and component), addition inducing refusal, and capability retention on benchmarks.
No independent evaluation; only one model is reported, with targets optimized on the same metric.

record.verdict_notes: This is a fork of p-e-w/heretic, with 0 stars. The evidence is the README only. The single-model table shows the abliteration tool works on Gemma 3 12B, which is anecdotally consistent with V2. But the numbers are the optimizer's own objective values, have no uncertainty estimates, and are platform-dependent. They are better treated as T4 tool performance than as a test. The README's note that interpolated directions often beat any single layer's direction is an informal remark with no data, not a V4 result.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not test adding the direction to induce refusals, the exact projection of the direction out of every layer and position, or general capabilities directly. KL divergence from the original on harmless prompts is reported, not a capability benchmark.
Only the reported Gemma 3 12B instruct checkpoints are evaluated; no other released models or settings are reported.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training against ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
